checkpoints.question: Why can `localhost` name a different system when the same command text runs elsewhere?
checkpoints.model_answer: The current network context determines `localhost`: a base-station shell refers to the base station, while a shell on either a physical or virtual Duckiedrone refers to that Duckiedrone. A service shell refers to its own service environment.

checkpoints.question: Why can a service respond at `127.0.0.1:PORT` but not at `DUCKIEDRONE_NAME.local:PORT`, where `PORT` is the documented port number for the service and `DUCKIEDRONE_NAME` is the name of your Duckiedrone?
checkpoints.model_answer: A service bound to `127.0.0.1` accepts connections only from the same network context. A request from another computer arrives through a different network interface.
